body.statement: Under assignment positivity, the four marginal binomial sampling laws, validation transport, and the confidence-budget condition, \[\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}\Pr_P\{K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\}\ge1-\beta.\] No mutual-independence condition on \(T_0,T_1,V_1,V_0\) is required. Coverage holds uniformly through optimizer ties, marginal contacts, and collapsed faces. Moreover, each endpoint of \(I_{\beta}\) is computable by a four-region profiling rule: the nontrivial root region uses the ten-point map, the two fractional regions use polygon vertices, and the constant region uses a feasibility check. Applied to \(\mathrm{def:kill-test-witness}\), the lower projection retains the legal edge value \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed precision.
body.justification: Exact primitive inversion avoids branchwise bootstrap failures and remains valid at every nonsmooth contact.
body.gap: GabrielSachsJensen2024 evaluates bootstrap coverage, documents regular-bootstrap undercoverage near boundaries, and reports a conservative \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) correction; FanPark2010 and KaidoMolinariStoye2019 provide adjacent clean-bound and generic projection inference. None gives exact simultaneous validation-binomial projection through the finite contact-complete shared-assay evaluator.
body.consumer: A prospective BNT162b2-style endpoint study with a blinded validation substudy obtains a uniformly valid confidence set for its full true-channel benefit interval.
body.proof_tex:
For each primitive, let \(E_0,E_1,E_s,E_c\) denote the event that its Clopper--Pearson interval contains its true probability.  The cited exact-coverage result and the four marginal binomial assumptions give
\[
 \Pr(E_0^c)\leq\beta_0,\quad
 \Pr(E_1^c)\leq\beta_1,\quad
 \Pr(E_s^c)\leq\beta_s,\quad
 \Pr(E_c^c)\leq\beta_c.
\]
The pointwise indicator inequality
\[
 \mathbf 1_{(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)^c}
 \leq \mathbf 1_{E_0^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_1^c}
      +\mathbf 1_{E_s^c}+\mathbf 1_{E_c^c}
\]
and the confidence-budget assumption imply
\[
 \Pr(E_0\cap E_1\cap E_s\cap E_c)\geq1-\beta.
\]
No independence was used.  On this event, validation transport and channel compatibility put the true tuple \((q_0,q_1,u,v)\) in \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\).  Hence, for every \(\theta\in[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), its compatible root is in the projected image \(I_{\beta}\).  Monotonicity in \(\theta\) shows that their image is precisely
\[
 K^{\star}=[b_{\theta_U}(u,v),b_{\theta_L}(u,v)],
\]
so \(K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\).  The argument is pointwise for every compatible law and therefore proves the displayed infimum coverage.  It involves no uniqueness of an optimizer, differentiability of a moving face, or positive dimension of the feasible polytope; ties, contacts, and collapsed faces are consequently covered.

It remains to expose the promised finite computation.  Write \(Q_a=[\ell_a,h_a]\), and let \(R\) be the rectangle obtained by intersecting the validation intervals with the fixed channel rectangle and changing coordinates from \(c\) to \(u=1-c\).  A channel admits some feasible trial risks exactly when it belongs to
\[
 D_Q=R\cap\{u\leq\min(h_0,h_1),\ v\geq\max(\ell_0,\ell_1),\ v-u\geq\kappa\}.
\]
For a fixed channel, the margin monotonicities profile the risks as
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
&\widetilde q_0&\widetilde q_1&\theta\\ \hline
\text{lower endpoint}&\min(h_0,v)&\max(\ell_1,u)&\theta_U\\
\text{upper endpoint}&\max(\ell_0,u)&\min(h_1,v)&\theta_L.
\end{array}
\]
For the lower endpoint, a feasible channel with \(v\leq h_0\) makes \(p_0=1\), while one with \(u\geq\ell_1\) makes \(p_1=0\); in either case \(b=0\).  Feasibility of these two clipped polygons is an exact finite linear check.  If neither exists, all of \(D_Q\) has \(v>h_0\) and \(u<\ell_1\), so the risks are fixed at \((h_0,\ell_1)\) and the ten-point theorem computes the lower endpoint.

For the upper endpoint, split \(D_Q\) by the two lines \(u=\ell_0\) and \(v=h_1\).  On the four closed regions the profiled objective is, respectively,
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
u\leq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1&b_{\theta_L}(\ell_0,h_1;u,v)\\
u\geq\ell_0,\ v\geq h_1&(h_1-u)/(v-u)\\
u\leq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1&(v-\ell_0)/(v-u)\\
u\geq\ell_0,\ v\leq h_1&1.
\end{array}
\]
The first region uses the ten-point map and the last needs only a feasibility check.  On either fractional region the denominator is at least \(\kappa>0\).  If a polygon point is \(z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i\), where \(z_i\) are its vertices, then a ratio of affine numerator \(N\) and positive affine denominator \(G\) satisfies
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{G(z)}
 =\sum_i\frac{\lambda_iG(z_i)}{\sum_k\lambda_kG(z_k)}
       \frac{N(z_i)}{G(z_i)}.
\]
It is thus a convex combination of its vertex values, so its extrema occur at vertices.  This proves the four-region rule, including all shared boundaries by harmless duplication.

For the kill-test data, the lower profile fixes
\[
 \widetilde q_0=0.4000678118,qquad
 \widetilde q_1=0.3318863111,qquad
 \theta=0.9016929770.
\]
The point \((u,v)=(0.0395824405,0.4886211008)\) lies in the calibration rectangle, satisfies both margin inequalities, and has
\[
 v-u=0.4490386603>\kappa=0.4490386602.
\]
It is the retained vertex where the left channel edge meets the informativeness boundary to the displayed input precision.  Substitution in the stable quadratic formula gives
\[
 p_0=0.802793619282\ldots,qquad
 p_1=0.650954798424\ldots,qquad
 b=0.132058055576\ldots.
\]
Equivalently, treating every displayed input as its terminating decimal rational, substitution into \(F\) gives opposite signs at \(0.1320580555\) and \(0.1320580556\), while \(F_b>0\); hence the root lies between them.  Thus the projected lower search necessarily retains \(0.1320580555\) to the displayed truncation precision.
